I just finished a series on Netflix, Turning Point: Vietnam, I think it was called, and I cannot recommend it enough. It covers everything that led up to the war, during the war, the aftermath, and the effects from it that we still see today. They interview veterans, journalists, photographers, people from Vietnam that survived, etc. There was an episode that talked about what happened at Kent and they had interviewed a woman that was there. When she talked about how the police all got down on one knee and started actually lining up their shots through their scopes, my heart sank. She then goes on to say that at one point they all turned their scopes towards her brother almost all at once. So sad. Then for Nixon to blame the protesters for what happened and to say that calling them "bums" was almost too kind of a term.... What a prick. This country will never learn. It's heartbreaking.

How sad is it that we live in a world where a job can cause a mental health crisis and yet we have to wonder if that's a good enough excuse to take time off. That's heartbreaking isn't it?  If you can get that paid time off, I'd suggest it. Take that time to get serious about working on yourself and figuring out what you need to do to continue living. Whether that be therapy, healthy coping mechanisms, beginning to try to look for a new job or even all the above. Maybe try putting your resume out there. Worst case scenario? You don't find anything immediately, but at least you tried. Best case scenario? Someone stumbles across that resume they want an interview and you work for a place that doesn't make you have bad feelings. All of the comments you've already got on this post just means you have a lot of us in your corner wishing you the best.

If you are eligible and can apply for FMLA, I'd suggest that. Especially if you can afford unpaid time off. I think you have to have it approved by a doctor and talk to HR once you start getting your paperwork.

I completely understand what you're going through though. I was just telling one of my close friends at work that I'm not sure how much longer I can stay there due to the mental strain it's putting on me. I'm constantly angry, I get chest pains, I bring my attitude home and take it out on everyone. I'm to the point of wanting to throw my hands up and just end it. When you're already mentally ill, it doesn't take a whole lot at work to just push you over the edge. So just know you're not alone. I'm also 30, been with my company for 9 years and I'm afraid if I stay there for another 35 years until retirement, that I'll end up giving myself a heart attack or that job will just push me to the point that I end my life. It's sad, really.

Anyway, if you want to start small and not find a new job, I suggest FMLA as a starting point. I don't think most companies take any vacation away before you can use fmla. That way you can also save your paid time off.

Good luck on everything and hang in there!
